newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND MUST TARGET BUDGET SURPLUS THIS DECADE - PM.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND MUST TARGET BUDGET SURPLUS THIS DECADE - PM.

text.p: Finland should target a budget surplus this decade to create a buffer for worse times, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Thursday.
Reaching balance was still possible this decade, Lipponen told a news conference and said he hoped it would happen.
"Whether we can reach balance and a surplus this decade, I would just say that 'hopefully'," he said.

"This should be the target, since we cannot really, as responsible people, as the government and parliament, approve of the idea of going into a recession, should one come, with a budget deficit and much debt," he said.
"We must create a buffer for the future."
At end-July, Finland's state debt stood at 428.1 billion markka, up 2.6 billion from a month earlier.

Asked to comment on the chances of income tax cuts in combination with the autumn's round of pay talks, Lipponen said the government would keep in mind that reaching a moderate pay deal was a top-priority matter, but he added that it was too early to say whether a moderate pay deal could justify lower taxes at the expense of a higher deficit.
"The starting point has to be that we are prepared to seek a corresponding leeway from the budget," Lipponen said.
Experts agree that a moderate pay deal is key for keeping Finnish inflation at its current moderate level, and many say that a comprehsive national pay deal is the best way to moderation.

The head of a leading Finnish union lobby, the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK), said earlier that pay talks for a settlement starting late this year or at the turn of the year could be held in October-November.
